reviewer_reference: Package audit (not raised by reviewer; affects R1 points 1–2 denominators)
reviewer_quote: “594 of the 1,615 patients still had unknown 30-day status”
issue_title: Repeated unique_code groups need an approved reconciliation rule
evidence_locations: workbook unique_code column; stroke_project/src/s02_clean.py:24, s03_cohort.py:29, s12_extended.py:27, s14_expert_modeling.py:112, s15_robustness.py:129
current_evidence: Recalculated: 38 repeated-identifier groups (all pairs), 76 rows, 38 excess rows; 35 groups have conflicting non-missing values (median 19 differing fields); 1 exact full-row duplicate group. The dictionary describes unique_code as a per-patient identifier (initials + admission date).
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: The code keeps the first row in four stages without a documented rule. Whether the pairs are re-entries, corrected records, two admissions or two patients is not established by the package.
scientific_risk_if_unresolved: Cohort size, event counts, the 1,615 denominator and every model result depend on the rule; keep-first can select the wrong record systematically.
required_action: Obtain the registry's reconciliation rule (Q8). Until then: aggregate conflict matrix; a documented, evidence-based rule (sex/age conflict ⇒ two patients; outcome-field conflict ⇒ outcome unresolved) with keep-first and exclude-conflicts as labelled sensitivity scenarios; cohort totals marked provisional.
analysis_specification: Population: all 1,653 rows. Output: conflict matrix by field category (dates, LOS, outcome, disposition, demographics, admission predictors, follow-up). Sensitivity: primary rule vs keep-first vs exclude-conflicts; report n, events, AUROC under each.
registry_questions: Q10/Q11 of the registry request (source adjudication of the 38 groups)
author_questions: Approve the interim rule and the sensitivity presentation
manuscript_destinations: Methods 2.2; Results 3.1; Appendix duplicate tables; Limitations
acceptance_criteria: Rule documented and applied by code with per-group evidence; conflicting outcomes never forced; three scenario cohorts reported; manuscript states that source adjudication is pending.
independent_verification_procedure: Re-derive group counts from the workbook with an independent script; check that no row is dropped silently (source-row ids preserved).
notes_and_limitations: Analytically reducible to a transparent rule + sensitivity; registry confirmation remains outstanding.

issue_title: Replace keep="first" deduplication in all four pipeline stages
current_evidence: Five call sites use drop_duplicates(keep='first') (one without keep argument, default first).
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: Arbitrary, undocumented, applied inconsistently to different frames.
scientific_risk_if_unresolved: Row choice may differ between stages, so cohorts in different tables are not the same patients.
required_action: Single reconciliation function applied once, before any analysis, with a logged decision per group.
analysis_specification: Function reconcile(rows) -> patients with decision ∈ {merge, split (collision), unresolved-outcome, drop-blank}; unit tests on synthetic pairs.
acceptance_criteria: No drop_duplicates on identifiers anywhere; test asserts every source row maps to exactly one patient or a logged exclusion.

issue_title: Reconcile the Pandas vs openpyxl LOS/date diagnostic counts
evidence_locations: workbook columns Date of entry, Release date, Length of hospitalization; review_audit/package_facts_recalculated.json
current_evidence: Independent recalculation (pandas 3.0.5, openpyxl 3.1.5): both parsers give 1488 complete pairs, 821 equal, 667 differing, 23 negative intervals among pairs with numeric LOS and 24 negative intervals among all datetime pairs. All entry/release cells are true Excel datetimes (number format mm-dd-yy; no text dates, no formulas). Emulating the pandas < 3.0 nanosecond Timestamp limit (max year 2262) reproduces the earlier 1,486 / 821 / 665 / 22 figures exactly: the two rows lost are the pairs with release year 2916 and entry year 3016.
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: The earlier 1,486/665/22 counts came from a pandas version that silently converts out-of-range years to NaT. Nothing else differs.
scientific_risk_if_unresolved: Without reconciliation, two impossible-date rows could be treated as missing dates instead of invalid dates.
required_action: Adopt the openpyxl counts (1,488/821/667/23; 24 negative overall) as the diagnostic; flag the two impossible-year rows explicitly as invalid dates (not missing); pin pandas ≥ 3.0 or add an explicit year-range guard.
analysis_specification: Date validity rule: entry year within registry span 2010–2023, release year ≤ 2024; out-of-range ⇒ invalid flag; never altered.
acceptance_criteria: Script reproduces both figure sets and names the cause; unit test with a year-3016 synthetic cell.
independent_verification_procedure: Re-run the audit script on the original workbook.
notes_and_limitations: Resolved analytically in this audit; no registry input needed for the parser question itself.

reviewer_quote: “reconstruct missing 30-day mortality outcomes using in-hospital death, length of stay”
issue_title: Recorded LOS and date-derived interval disagree in 667 of 1,488 pairs; authoritative field unknown
evidence_locations: workbook; dictionary row 'Length of hospitalization' typed 'date'
current_evidence: 667 disagreements; of these most differ by one day (inclusive vs elapsed counting) and 174 by more than one day (prior audit). Dictionary labels LOS as type 'date' although cells are integers.
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: Units/calculation rule of LOS undocumented; which field is authoritative is unknown.
scientific_risk_if_unresolved: Day-30 classification of stays near the boundary could flip.
required_action: Ask Q6/Q7. Interim rule: use date-derived elapsed days when both dates valid and 0–120 d, otherwise recorded LOS; when the two fall on opposite sides of day 30 and no month-1 status exists, leave the outcome unresolved; report the agreement table.
analysis_specification: Report distribution of (recorded − derived) by disposition; count boundary conflicts.
acceptance_criteria: Rule stated in Methods; boundary conflicts counted and left unresolved; sensitivity unaffected by small changes.
notes_and_limitations: Interim rule is transparent; custodian confirmation outstanding.

issue_title: Negative intervals and impossible years must be flagged, never corrected
current_evidence: 24 release-before-entry intervals (23 with numeric LOS); one entry year 3016, one release year 2916; prior audit: 22 release-before-entry within registry years.
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: Source of the errors unknown (typing, field swap).
required_action: Flag; exclude from stay derivation; ask Q11 for source check.

issue_title: Parse the dictionary correctly (cp1252, ';') and record dictionary–workbook mismatches
current_evidence: 256 variables; 16,128 blank trailing lines; 242 labels match workbook headers exactly; 14 dictionary labels absent from the workbook (incl. patient name, 2 phone numbers, follow-up location, first release date) and 9 workbook headers differ by spelling; 94 variables have no type; LOS typed 'date'; no value codes anywhere; content identical to the xlsx dictionary received 2 Nov.
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: Type labels unreliable; no codes; no units.
required_action: Dictionary audit as a pipeline stage; treat types as advisory; report mismatches.

issue_title: Undocumented codes: death1 '9', death3 '3'/'9', LOS 99, cause-of-death '0'/'9'/'99', disposition 'Other' and '6'
current_evidence: death1: 1 × '9'; death3: 2 × '3', 1 × '9'; cause of death: 73 × '0', 4 × '9', 1 × '99'; disposition: 159 × 'Other', 1 × '6'.
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: No codebook.
scientific_risk_if_unresolved: Converting codes to survival or death would be fabrication.
required_action: Treat as unknown (grade X); ask Q5/Q12.
acceptance_criteria: Codes never mapped to a status without a documented rule.

reviewer_quote: “The authors must clearly define what "death1" actually represents”
issue_title: Meaning and time origin of death1 (Month 1)
evidence_locations: dictionary row décès1; sibling rows barthel1 … rank_m12; workbook duration followed1
current_evidence: Dictionary: death1 = 'Death at Month 1, recording if the patient passed away within the first month'; month-1…12 assessments described as '… after the stroke'; duration followed1 = 1 (2010–16) or 30 (2017–19), 0 in 2021–23. No explicit time origin for death1; no codes; no date of death. Data: in-hospital deaths within 30 d recorded as death1 = Yes in 80/82 (2010–12) vs 3/167 (2015–23).
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: Time origin only implicit (stroke onset); meaning of 'No' unknown (OUTCOME-TIME-002); completion changed over time although the definition did not.
scientific_risk_if_unresolved: An admission-origin 30-day endpoint is not directly established; events recorded only in death1 (33) depend on the assumption that a month-1 death falls within 30 days of admission.
required_action: Define the endpoint explicitly (death within 30 d of admission, including in-hospital death); state assumptions A1 (disposition 'death' = in-hospital death) and A2 (post-discharge death1 = Yes within 30 d of admission); carry provenance per label; strict (A2 events unresolved) and stroke-anchored (death1 = No with long onset-to-arrival delay unresolved) sensitivity endpoints; ask Q1–Q3.
analysis_specification: Label classes E1/E2/N1–N4/U with evidence grades; nested-CV AUROC under primary, strict, observed-only and stroke-anchored endpoints.
author_questions: Accept the endpoint wording 'registry-recorded first-month outcome under stated assumptions'
acceptance_criteria: Definition quoted verbatim from the dictionary; assumptions stated and tested; no label reaches 'confirmed' grade until a time origin is documented.
independent_verification_procedure: Check manuscript text against the dictionary file.
notes_and_limitations: Dictionary supports but does not verify the time origin; the reviewer's day-40 example would be recorded as death1 = No under the dictionary definition.

issue_title: Meaning of death1 = No (confirmed alive vs not reached vs no death recorded)
current_evidence: Not stated.
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: A 'No' entered when the patient was not reached would be a false survival label.
required_action: Ask Q3; keep 'No' as grade R (recorded, time origin not established); report later-contact agreement as indirect evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Manuscript states the uncertainty; grade R retained.

reviewer_quote: “reconstruct the 30-day outcome based on the actual date of death”
issue_title: Availability of actual dates of death
current_evidence: No date-of-death column in workbook or dictionary; 'Release date' exists for 1,513 rows; cause of death recorded for 219 patients with disposition 'death' (217) or other (2).
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: Whether an authorised source outside the workbook holds dates of death is unknown.
scientific_risk_if_unresolved: Without dates, 33 post-discharge events remain assumption-dependent.
required_action: Ask Q4/Q12 for dates (or contact dates) of the 33 post-discharge deaths; never infer a death date from cause-of-death, LOS or release date except under A1 for in-hospital deaths.
acceptance_criteria: Either dates obtained and endpoint re-derived, or absence stated.

issue_title: Meaning of Release date and LOS when disposition is 'death' (assumption A1)
evidence_locations: workbook: 217 of 219 recorded causes of death belong to disposition 'death'; dictionary devenir = 'Outcome after leaving the UNV'
current_evidence: Consistent with release date = date of death for in-hospital deaths, but not documented.
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: If release date is not the death date, in-hospital death timing (E1) is wrong.
required_action: Ask Q5 (release date for deceased); keep A1 stated and tested (strict analyses unaffected because E1 uses the same stay).
acceptance_criteria: A1 stated with its supporting evidence.

reviewer_reference: Additional: Incomplete Reporting of Reconstruction Assumptions, bullet 1
reviewer_quote: “Length-of-stay ≤ 30 days for in-hospital deaths: Why 30 days? What is the distribution of length-of-stay for in-hospital deaths?”
issue_title: Justify the day-30 boundary and report the stay distribution of in-hospital deaths
current_evidence: The window is the estimand (death within 30 d of admission), not a tuning choice; an in-hospital death after day 30 is a non-event by definition. Stay distribution by disposition can be computed.
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: Not reported in the June manuscript.
scientific_risk_if_unresolved: Reviewer may read the boundary as arbitrary.
required_action: Report stay by disposition (median, IQR, days 28–32, >30) and the number of in-hospital deaths at the boundary; remove the 21–35-day window sweep (it answers no question).
analysis_specification: Table: disposition × stay summary; boundary counts.

reviewer_quote: “Discharged alive after >30 in-hospital days → alive at 30 days … should be justified with data on the distribution of length-of-stay.”
issue_title: Rule 'discharged alive after > 30 d ⇒ alive at day 30' — justify with chronology and stay data
current_evidence: Under A1 and valid dates, discharge alive on day d > 30 implies survival to day 30 by chronology; affects few patients (5 in the re-derived cohort).
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: Not justified in text; depends on LOS validity.
required_action: State the chronological argument; report count; exclude boundary conflicts.

reviewer_reference: Additional: reconstruction assumptions, bullet 3; R1 point 3 (time-to-event)
reviewer_quote: “How many patients had later follow-up? What was the completeness of later follow-up?”
issue_title: Semantics and completeness of death3/6/9 and their use as survival evidence
evidence_locations: dictionary rows décès3/6/9 ('passed away within three/six/nine months'); workbook counts
current_evidence: Dictionary wording is cumulative ('within'); later contacts recorded for 705 eligible patients (44.6%; 87% of 2010–12 admissions, ≤ 16% from 2017); they supply 20 survival labels (N4) in the prior re-derivation.
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: Whether 'No' at month 3 certifies survival through month 1 (cumulative) is implied, not stated.
scientific_risk_if_unresolved: If point-specific, N4 labels are unsupported.
required_action: Ask Q9; report completeness by period; sensitivity without N4 labels.

reviewer_quote: “or time-to-event approaches”
issue_title: Units and meaning of duration followed1/3/6/9
evidence_locations: workbook counts: duration followed1 ∈ {1 (488), 30 (58), 0 (27), …}; followed3 ∈ {3 (441), 1 (149), 90 (50), …}; followed6 {6, 1, 180}; followed9 {9, 1, 270}
current_evidence: Values are nominal visit months or the same in days (30/90/180/270); they are schedule labels, not observed event or censoring times. 0 in 2021–23 unexplained.
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: Not event times.
scientific_risk_if_unresolved: Survival analysis on these fields would invent event times.
required_action: Ask Q10; document as nominal; see EPI-SURV-001.
acceptance_criteria: Manuscript states the fields are nominal schedule values.

reviewer_reference: Additional: reconstruction assumptions (all bullets); R1 point 2
reviewer_quote: “The transparent, provenance-tagged outcome reconstruction”
issue_title: Report the number of labels assigned by each rule with provenance and evidence grade
current_evidence: Reproducible from the workbook; the June counts were reproduced exactly by independent code in the audit workspace.
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: June rules used 'Other' disposition and release dates as survival evidence; labels lacked evidence grades.
scientific_risk_if_unresolved: Readers cannot judge which labels rest on assumptions.
required_action: Provenance table (class, n, provenance, grade) and transition table June → revised.
acceptance_criteria: Every label has a class and grade; counts sum to eligible.

issue_title: Manuscript statement of telephone follow-up at days 7, 14 and 30 after discharge is unsupported
evidence_locations: original_june2026_source/main.tex line 92; dictionary (phone-number fields exist, no procedure); stroke_project documentation (no individual telephone records)
current_evidence: Dictionary lists two phone-number fields and a follow-up location (none in the workbook); no procedure, contact dates or completed-contact indicators exist.
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: Statement is not evidenced and conflicts with the month-based follow-up fields.
required_action: Remove the statement; describe follow-up as month-1/3/6/9 status fields of undocumented procedure; ask Q11.
author_questions: Confirm what the follow-up procedure actually was
acceptance_criteria: Statement removed; procedure described as undocumented unless confirmed.

reviewer_quote: “33.8% represents only the proportion of deaths among patients for whom a reconstructed outcome could be obtained”
issue_title: 33.8% must not be reported as registry-wide mortality; report denominators and bounds
current_evidence: Agreed. Re-derivation shows the labelled subset is upper-biased (deaths almost always labelled, survivors only when follow-up recorded), so 33.8% is neither the registry rate nor a conservative estimate.
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: June text calls it the 'true' corrected rate.
scientific_risk_if_unresolved: Central epidemiological claim wrong in direction.
required_action: Report labelled-subset mortality with its selection; deterministic bounds (all unresolved alive/dead) with denominators; in-hospital 30-d mortality among known dispositions; IPW and delta-adjusted estimates as model-based, assumption-dependent figures.
analysis_specification: Bounds: deaths/eligible and (deaths+unresolved)/eligible; IPW per EPI-SEL-003; delta per EPI-SEL-004.
acceptance_criteria: No sentence presents a labelled-subset rate as the registry rate; bounds labelled deterministic, not CIs.

reviewer_quote: “missing-outcome exclusion under-ascertains mortality by ~14 percentage points”
issue_title: Withdraw the 14-point under-ascertainment figure
current_evidence: Observed-only 20.2% vs reconstructed 33.8%; both are biased (in opposite directions) so their difference is not an under-ascertainment magnitude.
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: Claim rests on treating 33.8% as truth.
required_action: Replace with the two-direction bias statement and bounds.

reviewer_quote: “their NIHSS and mRS scores were significantly lower than those of patients included in the analysis”
issue_title: Compare labelled and unresolved patients on admission variables with effect sizes
current_evidence: Differences exist (NIHSS median 7 vs 10; mRS 3 vs 4; more missing NIHSS; concentrated in 2017–23; 20% without disposition).
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: June reported p-values only.
required_action: Standardised mean differences and proportions by labelling status, period and disposition; interpret as evidence against MCAR, not proof of MNAR.

reviewer_quote: “further develop a prediction model for outcome ascertainability”
issue_title: Ascertainability (observation) model using baseline-time variables
current_evidence: Feasible: logistic model of P(labelled) on admission variables with missingness indicators, period, disposition and stay > 30 d (post-admission variables are legitimate in an observation model, never as predictors).
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: Positivity fails for patients without a recorded disposition (P ≈ 0.002).
required_action: Fit; report discrimination, probability distribution, positivity diagnostics; restrict IPW target population to patients with a recorded disposition.

reviewer_quote: “consider inverse-probability weighting”
issue_title: IPW estimate of registry mortality with weight diagnostics; no claim that IPW solves MNAR
current_evidence: Feasible under conditional exchangeability given the observation-model covariates; weights truncated at the 99th percentile; bootstrap re-estimating weights.
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: Assumption untestable.
required_action: Report weighted mortality with bootstrap CI, ESS, truncation; state assumptions; IPW-weighted model evaluation as sensitivity.
acceptance_criteria: Assumptions stated; ESS and truncation reported.

reviewer_quote: “missing-not-at-random sensitivity analyses”
issue_title: MNAR sensitivity: delta-adjustment / tipping point
current_evidence: Pattern-mixture delta-adjustment feasible: unresolved patients assigned reference risks, odds multiplied by δ ∈ [0.25, 8]; tipping δ at which registry mortality equals the labelled-subset rate.
required_action: Implement; report curve and tipping δ.
acceptance_criteria: Curve and tipping δ reported with assumptions.

reviewer_quote: “or time-to-event approaches”
issue_title: Feasibility of discrete-time / interval-censored survival analysis
current_evidence: No event dates; no censoring dates; follow-up durations are nominal schedule values; month-1 status completion changed over time. Interval-censoring would require knowing that each 'No' is a verified alive contact at a known time (OUTCOME-TIME-002) and that deaths recorded at month 3–9 fall in a known interval.
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: Conditions for valid survival analysis not met with supplied fields.
required_action: Write a feasibility report; do not implement; state in Methods.
acceptance_criteria: Feasibility report lists each condition and its status.
notes_and_limitations: Re-assess if the registry supplies contact dates.

reviewer_reference: Additional: Circularity in Outcome Reconstruction and Temporal Validation
reviewer_quote: “The later-period improvement may partly reflect the reconstruction's dependence on in-hospital data that became more complete over time”
issue_title: Time-varying ascertainment, label-source composition and the circularity argument
current_evidence: Month-1 field completion fell from 91% (2010–12) to 7–46% (2017–23); in-hospital deaths were no longer written to death1 from 2015; disposition completeness fell in 2020–23. The observed-only test set had 7 events (June) so its AUROC was uninformative rather than 'collapsed'.
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: June interpreted the AUROC difference as proof of an artefact.
required_action: Report ascertainment proportion, label-source composition, missingness and case mix by period; withdraw the 'resolves the collapse' interpretation; state that the reconstruction depends on fields whose completeness changed.

reviewer_quote: “(from AUROC 0.72 to 0.85)”
issue_title: Reconstructed and observed-only temporal analyses used different cut-offs (2016-08-24 vs 2015-12-26)
evidence_locations: 14_temporal.csv (train < 2016-08-24, n_test 306, 125 events); 15_temporal_observed.csv (train < 2015-12-26, n_test 241, 7 events); s14_expert_modeling.py:121 (70% of ordered dates within each labelled cohort)
current_evidence: Cut-off = 70th percentile of dates within each labelled cohort, so it differs by endpoint.
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: Not a like-for-like comparison.
required_action: One cut-off fixed in advance from all eligible admissions (outcome-independent), applied to every endpoint; report n, events, ascertainment and label composition per period.
acceptance_criteria: Same cut-off date in every temporal table.

reviewer_quote: “"Generalises across time" is too strong for a temporal split within the same centre.”
issue_title: Internal temporal validation is not external validation
current_evidence: Agreed.
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: Wording.
required_action: Describe as internal temporal evaluation; state that external validation is required.

reviewer_quote: “report the difference in AUC with its 95% confidence interval”
issue_title: Paired AUROC difference with 95% CI for every model comparison
evidence_locations: 14_paired_delong.csv (full 0.822 vs clinical 0.848, p = 0.171; no CI); src/utils.py delong_paired_test
current_evidence: Code returns p only.
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: No interval.
scientific_risk_if_unresolved: Logical error identified by the reviewer.
required_action: Paired DeLong difference and CI (covariance of paired AUCs) in nested CV (pooled OOF) and temporal test; paired bootstrap check.
acceptance_criteria: Every comparison has difference and CI; unit test against hand-computed example.

reviewer_quote: “It does not demonstrate equivalence … a pre-specified margin with clinical justification is required.”
issue_title: Remove equivalence/'matches' claims
current_evidence: No margin was pre-specified.
required_action: Remove; state 'imprecise and compatible with no difference'.

reviewer_quote: “If the calibration method was selected based on results from the test set, then the test set can no longer be considered an independent evaluation set.”
issue_title: Calibration fitting/selection protocol and test-set lock
evidence_locations: s12_extended.py lines 70–84: Platt and isotonic fitted on validation predictions, both evaluated on the test set; headline wording chose Platt after seeing test Brier/HL
current_evidence: Fitting was on validation data; selection/presentation used test results.
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: Test-set independence compromised for the calibration claim.
required_action: Primary model not recalibrated; Platt/isotonic as sensitivity fitted by inner CV within each training fold; no selection on test; document roles of every partition.
acceptance_criteria: No test-set quantity used for any choice; documented.

reviewer_quote: “a "Low" tier with 0% mortality and 0% deaths captured … the manuscript does not explain why the single-split tiers collapsed.”
issue_title: Empty Low tier: explain and replace data-driven tiers with pre-specified cut-points
evidence_locations: 10_risk_tiers.csv (Low: n = 0 in validation and test); s10_risk_clinical.py (cut-points searched on validation to capture deaths); 15_oof_tiers.csv uses fixed 0.15/0.50
current_evidence: Validation search chose a low cut-point below every predicted risk, so no patient was 'Low'; the OOF table used different fixed thresholds.
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: Two incompatible procedures.
required_action: Pre-specified absolute-risk cut-points (< 10%, ≥ 40%) applied to OOF and temporal predictions; report counts, deaths, mortality with CI, capture, patients per death; explain the collapse.

reviewer_quote: “The clinical utility of the tiers is asserted but not demonstrated.”
issue_title: Utility claims: decision curves as exploratory; tiers not recommended; pathway as hypothesis
current_evidence: Net benefit depends on prevalence, which is distorted by selection.
required_action: DCA unweighted and IPW-weighted, labelled exploratory; tiers not recommended; implications as hypothesis.

reviewer_reference: Additional: Missing Data Handling, bullet 2; package audit
reviewer_quote: “The imputation model is not described. What variables were included? Were auxiliary variables used? How many imputations?”
issue_title: Imputation description must match code: deterministic IterativeImputer (single-split) and median imputation (nested CV) are not MICE
evidence_locations: s05_split_impute.py:37 (IterativeImputer, BayesianRidge, max_iter 10, sample_posterior=False); s14_expert_modeling.py:48–52 (SimpleImputer median inside CV); June Methods ('MICE')
current_evidence: Single deterministic imputation called MICE; nested CV used a different method.
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: Wording/method mismatch.
required_action: One imputation procedure in every pipeline (iterative imputer inside each fold; variables and iterations stated; outcome excluded); multiple imputation (m = 5 posterior draws) as sensitivity with between-draw variability; never call single imputation MICE.
acceptance_criteria: Code and text identical in method, variables, iterations and m.

reviewer_reference: Additional: Missing Data Handling, bullets 1 and 3
reviewer_quote: “Is it missing at random (MAR), missing completely at random (MCAR), or missing not at random (MNAR)? … Other variables (e.g., CRP, creatinine) also have substantial missingness.”
issue_title: Missingness mechanism discussion and sensitivity for all materially incomplete predictors
current_evidence: Missingness associated with period and ascertainment (MCAR implausible); MAR working assumption; MNAR cannot be excluded.
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: June discussed NIHSS only.
required_action: Missingness table; indicator models for all predictors > 20% missing; model restricted to predictors < 10% missing; complete-NIHSS subset.

issue_title: XGBoost reported but absent from nested CV
current_evidence: Nested CV: LR, RF, HGB; XGBoost only in the single split.
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: Model lists differ between tracks.
required_action: Same model list in every validation design; report each model separately.

reviewer_quote: “The clinical-reference model is described as "parsimonious" but its exact specification is not fully reported.”
issue_title: Full specification of the clinical-reference comparator
current_evidence: Locally fitted logistic model on a few predictors.
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: Predictors, coding, fitting not stated; not iScore/PLAN.
required_action: State predictors (age, NIHSS, GCS, admission mRS, haemorrhagic, sex), unpenalised, linear, refitted per training set with the same imputation; state it is not iScore/PLAN and why those cannot be computed.

issue_title: Exclude post-baseline fields from predictors; splits at the patient level
current_evidence: June excluded LOS/disposition from predictors (leakage audit table); but repeat admissions cannot be linked because unique_code includes the admission date.
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: Patient-level linkage impossible.
scientific_risk_if_unresolved: Possible within-patient leakage across folds [NOT ESTABLISHED].
required_action: Predictor eligibility list in config; unit test; state the unit of analysis (admission) and the linkage limitation.

issue_title: Feature selection, scaling, imputation and tuning inside training folds only
evidence_locations: s06 (LASSO selection on the single training split); s14 pipeline (SelectFromModel inside Pipeline — correct)
current_evidence: Nested CV pipeline is leakage-free; single-split track selected 13 features by LASSO then reported EPV 18.5 on selected features.
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: EPV on selected features overstates sample adequacy.
required_action: No data-driven feature selection (all 27 candidates, L2 penalty tuned in inner CV); EPV on candidates; post hoc Riley sample-size check.
acceptance_criteria: No selection step; EPV on candidates.

reviewer_quote: “The Glasgow-to-NIHSS ratio is highlighted as a key predictor, but its clinical interpretation is speculative.”
issue_title: Treat the GCS/NIHSS ratio as exploratory; test whether it adds information
current_evidence: Ratio adds nothing beyond components in the re-derivation (0.861 vs 0.863).
what_is_wrong_or_unknown: Over-emphasised.
required_action: Remove from the main model; report as a sensitivity feature only; no mechanism claims.

reviewer_quote: “Spearman ρ = 0.70, which is moderate, not high.”
issue_title: Characterise rank concordance as moderate with an interval
current_evidence: Re-derived ρ = 0.56 (feature-bootstrap 0.17–0.80).
required_action: Report ρ with interval and call it moderate.

reviewer_quote: “LIME explanations (Figure 17) are presented for four cases, but there is no systematic evaluation of explanation stability or fidelity.”
issue_title: LIME cases: illustrative only or removed
current_evidence: No stability/fidelity testing.
required_action: Remove LIME cases (no systematic validation under the deadline); keep coefficient, permutation and SHAP descriptions with bootstrap rank frequencies.
acceptance_criteria: No LIME figure or stability claim.

reviewer_quote: “The manuscript conflates two distinct contributions”
issue_title: Separate the ascertainment finding from the modelling contribution
current_evidence: Agreed.
required_action: Two explicit questions in the Introduction; Results and Discussion follow the split; modelling contribution described as modest.

reviewer_quote: “The "as much as" overstates the modelling contribution.”
issue_title: Narrow the contribution statements
required_action: Rewrite.

reviewer_quote: “Priority claims require systematic review to substantiate.”
issue_title: Remove the 'first … model' priority claim
